decisions.rule: Company and Person are independent customer types; Branch is a Company subordinate, with its own facts, not an independent customer.
CRM activities may reference Branch as an attribution target, while Company remains the parent; activity-specific authorization and scope remain separate.
One Person may have multiple concurrent relationships with Companies and Branches in the same authorized Tenant scope; relationships do not duplicate identity.
A corporate contact is represented by Person, even without individual active commercial engagement; Contact stores communication channels, Relationship stores affiliation.
Potential matches generate an access-controlled warning and existing-record suggestion; authorized new records are allowed with a mandatory reason.
A user authorized for CUS-CREATE may override a probabilistic duplicate warning with a required reason and Audit obligation; no supervisor approval is required.
Ordinary duplicate override must not bypass a collision with a validated authoritative unique identifier; the identifier registry/scope and conflict resolution remain OPEN.
Record lifecycle is separate from commercial engagement/classification; commercial taxonomy is not fixed here.
Record states are ACTIVE, INACTIVE, ARCHIVED; after successful authorized creation and validation, initial state is ACTIVE.
ACTIVE -> INACTIVE may occur with ongoing activities preserved; initiating new activities is restricted by activity-specific policy.
ACTIVE/INACTIVE -> ARCHIVED is blocked until every applicable open activity/dependency is disposed of; unknown dependency outcome cannot be treated as clear.
ARCHIVED -> INACTIVE is the only restore transition; INACTIVE -> ACTIVE requires revalidation. Direct ARCHIVED -> ACTIVE is forbidden.
CUS-UPDATE permits authorized users to edit identity facts, including sensitive business identifiers, with revalidation and Audit; no separate supervisor approval.
CUS-UPDATE requires a record version; stale-version writes are rejected fully. No automatic merge or last-write-wins.
An edit reason is mandatory only for changes to sensitive identity identifiers and exceptional changes; routine edits do not require a reason. All durable updates retain Audit obligations.

Company legal/display name and Person given/family names are required for initial registration; system-issued stable identity and ACTIVE initial record status. Structured name parts and normalization rules require field-dictionary review.

Official Person and Company identifiers are optional at initial create; workflows requiring formal identity verification may require the identifier and qualifying verification. Neither phone nor email is mandatory at initial registration.

A sufficiently verified official identifier must be unique within its approved identity/issuer/Tenant scope; confirmed conflicts block create/update or confirmation and cannot be bypassed with probabilistic-match exception. Identifier namespace and technical unique key remain OPEN.

Formal identity verification is distinct from record lifecycle and commercial status. Its states are NOT_VERIFIED, VERIFIED, REQUIRES_REVERIFICATION; initial creation is NOT_VERIFIED unless a separate trusted verification occurs.

Both trusted external/system verification and evidence-backed manual verification by separately authorized actor are permitted; both produce attributable evidence/history and coordinated Audit obligations. Customer Domain remains final authoritative state writer.

decisions.topic: Manual verification and separation of duties
decisions.rule: An actor who created the customer may manually verify that customer if independently permitted in normal processes; sensitive processes require a different verifying actor. Sensitive-process catalog and permission grants remain OPEN.

No universal time-based identity verification expiry. Effective validity depends on underlying required evidence, material identity changes, trusted revocation, and evidence validity rules. Age alone does not invalidate VERIFIED.

Expiry/loss of validity of evidence necessary to substantiate an otherwise valid earlier verification, or a material change to identity facts supporting it, moves VERIFIED to REQUIRES_REVERIFICATION; successful new trusted verification returns VERIFIED.

If prior verification is proven fundamentally invalid (false/misattributed/invalid from outset), effective status becomes NOT_VERIFIED, including from REQUIRES_REVERIFICATION. Requires an independent new trusted verification for VERIFIED; never erase historical evidence.

Verification decisions preserve method (SYSTEM/MANUAL), source/issuer, verified actor/service, decision time, relevant identity revision, controlled evidence reference, reason and correlation. Protect sensitive evidence and retain histories subject to unresolved retention and disclosure rules.

Generic CUS-UPDATE must not directly set VERIFIED; trusted verification workflow authorizes and verifies actor or provider result, identity revision, duplicate collision, evidence and required durable Audit. Stale or ambiguous responses do not confer VERIFIED.

NOT_VERIFIED and REQUIRES_REVERIFICATION can coexist with ACTIVE Customer; any consuming operation requiring verified identity must check effective evidence validity before relying on VERIFIED, not assume status flag alone suffices.

Verification expiry/revocation preserves Customer ID, historical relationships and an auditable, provenance-bound record. Trusted fundamental invalidation cannot silently be ignored by sensitive consumers when persistence is temporarily unavailable; precise fail/recovery contract remains OPEN.

Each Person may have multiple concurrent Relationships with Company and/or Branch. Each independent role is represented by a distinct Relationship; roles/affiliations belong to Relationship, not to duplicate Person records.

Recommended conceptual Relationship fields: relationshipId, personId, targetType (COMPANY|BRANCH), targetId, roleCode, roleTitle, status, startDate, endDate, recordVersion, createdAt, updatedAt, endedReason, optional source/evidence reference. These are conceptual, not an approved schema or API.
Relationship lifecycle states are ACTIVE and ENDED (proposed for formal review). An ENDED historical Relationship is not reopened; a later recurrence of the same role is a separate Relationship.

Use the conceptual half-open interval [startDate, endDate): start inclusive, end exclusive, null end means open-ended, empty or backwards intervals are invalid. Effective usability considers status, interval, Person status, target status and permissions.
For the same Person, TargetType, TargetId and RoleCode, overlapping Relationship intervals are allowed only through a controlled exception with a warning, valid authority, mandatory reason and Audit.
Distinct role codes may overlap freely; the same role may overlap across different companies/targets; the same role in Company vs its Branch concerns different targets (different TargetId).

Same Person + same target + same role + overlapping intervals produces a warning. The user may select/use an existing Relationship instead of creating a new one. An authorized user may intentionally create/update an overlapping Relationship with a mandatory exception reason; no separate supervisor approval is required.
A reason is required for each newly authorized overlap decision; old reasons do not authorize all future changes automatically.
Even ENDED Relationship intervals participate in historical overlap detection.

Two cases are distinguished: (1) updating the same Relationship rejects stale record versions; (2) creating separate overlapping Relationships concurrently uses a consistent, authoritative overlap assessment. If the relevant conflict set changed after the user reviewed a warning, require re-evaluation before finalizing.
Idempotent retries must not produce unintended additional Relationship records. An intentional, approved overlap exception and an accidental duplicate request are distinct cases.

Overlap exception authorization does not bypass stale-version checks, Tenant isolation, input validation, or disclosure control. Avoid disclosing non-visible Relationship details through warning output.

The controlled-exception overlap policy SUPERSEDES any prior rule prohibiting all overlapping Relationships (same Person+target+role). No active absolute-overlap-prohibition rule remains; historical absolute-denial expectations, if imported later, are superseded.

Branch has only two independent record states: ACTIVE and INACTIVE. Branch does not have an independently managed ARCHIVED state. Effective operational availability depends on its own status, its parent Company lifecycle status, and applicable resource/action policy.

Deactivating Company does not automatically change stored Branch statuses. Deactivating Branch does not automatically modify Company or Person. Existing open activities remain available for permitted continuation; creating new activities is restricted if Branch or parent Company is effectively inactive.
Direct Branch reparenting is prohibited. branchId and companyId are immutable after creation.

When a Branch is genuinely transferred, create a new Branch under the target Company with a new Branch ID and deactivate the original. Do not transfer historical activities or Person Relationships automatically; historical activities remain attributed to the original Company/Branch. New Relationships and activity assignments use their own authorized operations. An optional succession reference between old and new branches may be proposed but must not transfer ownership/permissions.

Archiving Company requires resolution of applicable open dependencies across Company and Branches. Branch records and historical associations remain intact after Company archiving. Restoring Company does not automatically activate inactive Branches.

Branch is subordinate to Company (not an independent Customer), has its own stable ID and independently maintained data, and has exactly one Company parent whose ID is immutable after creation. Branches can have Person Relationships. Company/Branch references respect Tenant isolation.

decisions.topic: Audit obligations for durable and proposed operations
decisions.rule: Customer durable mutations honor existing coordinated persistent Audit obligations. Proposed independent Branch, Relationship and Verification operations require an auditability product requirement, with the precise operational contract still requiring formal approval.
Rejected validations, warnings, or read-only queries do not carry an assumed mandatory Audit rule unless supported by existing authoritative sources.
Prefer controlled references to sensitive evidence over copying entire identity documents or private identifiers into Audit logs.

A mandatory coordinated Audit failure must not result in a successful mutation being reported. Broker ACK or outbox publication alone is not authoritative Audit ingestion. Preserve version/concurrency safety and prevent stale provider results from silently overwriting newer verification states.

Similar names, shared phone numbers, or shared emails alone are not conclusive identity matches. Automatic merging of Customer records is not authorized. Distinguish an intentional duplicate-warning override from an accidental duplicate caused by retrying the same request. Avoid unauthorized disclosure of other customers/Tenant data through duplicate detection.

Address and Latin name are optional unless a specific consuming workflow requires them. Official identification may be required later by a workflow requiring formal identity verification. A structurally valid identifier is not automatically verified. Verified official identifiers must be unique within the formally defined identity scope; conclusive conflicts block the conflicting create/update. No silent assumption of global cross-Tenant identity deduplication.

Deactivation is allowed even with open activities; existing open activities and historical data remain intact. Starting new activities for INACTIVE customers is restricted per owning-module policy. Archiving must not delete Customer data, relationships, or audit history. Restoring an archived Customer must not automatically reopen historical activities/relationships.

Updating Company must not silently reparent Branches; updating Person must not silently alter unrelated Relationships. Converting Company into Person or vice versa is not supported as a normal CM-1 update. Routine edits of ARCHIVED records are not allowed (use authorized recovery). INACTIVE records may be corrected without automatically becoming ACTIVE.

A record can be ACTIVE and NOT_VERIFIED, and can be VERIFIED without automatically receiving access or operational authorization. Verification state never substitutes for resource authorization or membership.

decisions.topic: Verification time semantics and open items
decisions.rule: Effective time and recording time are recorded distinctly when relevant. The specific evidence-retention period, trusted-provider catalog, revocation dispute process, and detailed failure/recovery mechanism remain open.

Customer Master shall support a hybrid Relationship Role Catalog consisting of system-defined roles shared across authorized Tenants and Tenant-defined custom roles owned by their respective Tenant.

Role definitions represent organizational responsibilities and shall not grant IAM/RBAC permissions.

Each Role Definition shall have exactly one applicability scope:

- COMPANY
- BRANCH
- BOTH

New Relationship assignments shall be validated against the Role's current applicability scope.

Role Definitions shall support exactly two lifecycle states:

- ACTIVE
- INACTIVE

A newly created valid Role shall initially be ACTIVE.

An authorized actor may deactivate or reactivate a Role, subject to applicable validation and authorization.

decisions.topic: Immutable Identity and No Physical Deletion
decisions.rule:
The roleId and roleCode of a Role Definition shall remain immutable after creation.

Physical deletion of Role Definitions is not supported, including for Roles without existing Relationships.

Historical Role identities and references must be preserved.

Deactivating or reactivating a Role shall not automatically create, terminate, reactivate, delete, or modify any existing Relationship.

An INACTIVE Role shall not be available for new Relationship assignments.

Existing Relationships retain their individual statuses, temporal intervals, and historical references.

Authorized changes to a Role's applicability scope are permitted.

If the proposed change makes existing Relationships incompatible with the new scope:

1. The system shall evaluate the affected Relationships.
2. An impact warning shall be presented without unauthorized disclosure.
3. A mandatory business reason shall be captured.
4. Appropriate management authority shall be validated.
5. Existing Relationships shall remain unchanged.
6. The new scope shall govern subsequent Relationship assignments.
7. The change and its justification shall remain auditable.

A scope change shall not implicitly modify Person, Company, Branch, or Relationship state.

System Role Definitions shall be governed by the system catalog authority.

Tenant users shall not modify System Role Definitions.

Tenant Role Definitions shall be owned by a single Tenant and managed only by appropriately authorized actors within that Tenant.

Cross-Tenant Role access and references shall be prohibited unless explicitly authorized by a separate governing contract.

CUS-CREATE permission shall not by itself grant Role Catalog management authority.

Changes to Role titles, lifecycle status, or applicability scope shall preserve Role identity and historical Relationship references.

The controlled-exception Relationship overlap policy remains authoritative.

Role Catalog changes shall not bypass Relationship version checks, overlap authorization, Tenant isolation, or mandatory Audit obligations.

The exact Role reference contract and technical overlap key remain subject to formal design approval.

These 12 entries constitute the user-confirmed initial vocabulary, not a complete future role universe.
Their codes, Persian titles and scopes must be preserved exactly.
They are System Roles, available to authorized Tenants subject to effective selectability.
They describe organizational relationships, not security permissions or verified legal representation.
A Person can hold multiple independent roles under the existing Relationship rules.
Do not add an exclusive PRIMARY_CONTACT constraint or automatic authority for CEO, BOARD_MEMBER or any other role.
Existing identity and no-physical-deletion decisions remain authoritative.
Any proposed English titles are optional metadata, not user-confirmed values.
Do not assume a specific database seed format, globally fixed roleId values, migration or deployment mechanism.

An appropriately authorized actor within a Tenant may make an otherwise eligible System Role unavailable for new Relationship assignments in that Tenant and subsequently make it selectable again.

This Tenant-specific setting:
- Does not modify the global System Role Definition.
- Does not change global role status, scope, roleId or roleCode.
- Does not affect other Tenants.
- Does not create, modify, terminate, delete or reactivate existing Relationships.
- Does not hide historical Relationship references from otherwise authorized historical views.
- Does not grant any IAM/RBAC permission.
- Must be enforced by the authoritative Customer Domain, not merely by UI filtering.
- Requires validated Tenant context and applicable management authority; CUS-CREATE alone does not grant that authority.
- Does not permit Tenant users to edit System Role Definitions.
- Must not disclose another Tenant's settings or Relationships.

Effective eligibility for a new Relationship assignment requires all relevant conditions, including:
- The System Role is globally ACTIVE.
- The Role is applicable to the target COMPANY or BRANCH.
- The Role is selectable in the current Tenant.
- The actor has the required Relationship-operation authority.
- All existing Tenant, validation, concurrency and overlap guards pass.

A global INACTIVE state must not be bypassed by a Tenant setting.

Restoring Tenant selectability must not reactivate an INACTIVE global System Role or reopen an ENDED Relationship.

If a Role becomes non-selectable while a new assignment is being finalized, the operation must not accept an assignment against an invalid effective state. Exact concurrency enforcement remains a technical OPEN contract.

Important: Treat Tenant-specific unselectability as an assignment restriction, not as the same operation as global Role deactivation, and not as automatic deletion of role history.

Do not invent a Tenant override for global System Role lifecycle or applicableScope.

When a new Tenant is created, all globally ACTIVE System Roles are selectable by default for new Relationship assignments, subject to existing applicability, operation authorization and other guards.
When a new System Role is released, it is selectable by default in existing Tenants if globally ACTIVE.
Authorized Tenant managers may subsequently hide/unhide System Roles under CM1-PD-067.
Previously established Tenant hide/unhide settings must be preserved across System Catalog releases.
Global INACTIVE status always prevents new assignment, regardless of Tenant settings.
No existing Relationship is modified by default selectability or catalog publication.

Do not assume a specific storage representation, Tenant-provisioning process, migration strategy or default-setting materialization mechanism.

System Role codes are unique within the global System Catalog and reserved against Tenant-defined Roles.
A Tenant Role cannot use the same canonical roleCode as any existing or permanently reserved System Role code.
Tenant Role codes are unique within their owning Tenant, including inactive and historical reservations.
Separate Tenants may use the same custom roleCode. Their Role identities, ownership and Relationships remain independent.
All comparisons use the canonical normalized roleCode defined in CM1-PD-072.
Tenant isolation and disclosure restrictions remain mandatory.

Do not introduce a global prohibition on matching custom codes across independent Tenants.

Once assigned, a roleCode remains reserved within its applicable ownership/namespace scope, including when a Role becomes INACTIVE or is historical.
Deactivation and subsequent reactivation preserve roleId and roleCode.
Reserved codes must not be reassigned to a different Role.
No physical Role deletion is permitted under CM1-PD-061.
Historical Relationship references remain preserved.

Do not assume a particular tombstone table, index or retention implementation.

Before releasing a new System Role code, assess conflicts with existing and historically reserved Tenant Role codes across relevant Tenants.
If the proposed System code conflicts with an existing Tenant custom code, block publication of that new System Role until the conflict is resolved through an explicitly authorized process.
Never automatically rename, delete, convert or reassign a Tenant Role.
Never automatically migrate, terminate or modify existing Relationships.
Selecting a different code for the proposed System Role is a valid non-destructive conflict-resolution option.
Future resolution workflows, access authorities, disclosure rules and publication mechanics remain OPEN.

The product policy blocks release of the conflicting Role; do not infer that every unrelated catalog change or release must also be blocked.

Do not infer that the central catalog administrator may inspect Tenant-private data without authorization.

Normalize incoming roleCode by trimming leading/trailing whitespace and converting letters to uppercase.
Validate the normalized result against the allowed character set: ASCII A-Z, digits 0-9 and underscore (_).
The normalized roleCode length must be between 3 and 64 characters inclusive.
Use the canonical normalized value for uniqueness and reservation checks.
Preserve roleCode immutability after creation.

Examples:
- " technical_contact " → "TECHNICAL_CONTACT" (valid).
- "CEO" → "CEO" (valid).
- "ceo" → "CEO" (canonical collision with the System Role).
- "BRANCH-MANAGER" → invalid.
- "مدیر_شعبه" → invalid.
- A normalized code shorter than 3 or longer than 64 characters → invalid.

Do not silently add an unconfirmed requirement that the code must start with a letter, prohibit consecutive underscores, or prohibit a leading/trailing underscore unless separately approved.

Document any further lexical grammar or Unicode edge-case behavior as PROPOSED / OPEN, rather than USER-CONFIRMED.

Technical implementation of Unicode trim/uppercase semantics and input encoding remains subject to contract definition; acceptance tests must still enforce the confirmed allowed ASCII output.

Reason is optional for both Hide and Unhide.
Audit is mandatory.
Only authorized tenant catalog managers may perform these operations within their own tenant.
Record actor, tenant, role identity, previous and new selectability states, timestamp and optional reason.
Existing relationships and historical references remain unchanged.
Other tenants remain unaffected.
Unhide must not override global role inactivity, scope restrictions or authorization requirements.

roleId and roleCode remain immutable.
Authorized product governance may update system role labels, translations and descriptions through a controlled catalog release.
Authorized tenant catalog managers may update labels, translations and descriptions of their own custom roles.
Tenants cannot modify global System Role definitions.
Persian and English display labels may be maintained. Do not infer mandatory language fields or localization storage mechanisms.
Display labels are not unique identifiers.
Display metadata changes must preserve role identity and fundamental business semantics.
A materially different role requires a new role with a new roleCode.
Existing relationships must not be replaced, recreated or modified.
Audit is mandatory; reason is optional for ordinary metadata changes.
Preserve previous and new values.

Current relationships display the current valid role title, subject to authorization.
Historical events and Audit records preserve the role title applicable at the time of the event.
Renaming a role must not rewrite historical records.
Inactive and hidden roles remain visible in existing relationships and authorized historical records.
Stable roleId and roleCode must be preserved.
Tenant isolation and historical access authorization remain mandatory.
Temporal storage, versioning, snapshot mechanisms and API representation remain OPEN.

Separate three logical authority categories:

1. System catalog governance authority:
- Create System Roles.
- Update system display metadata.
- Change system role scope.
- Activate/deactivate System Roles.
- Publish controlled catalog revisions.

2. Authorized tenant catalog manager:
- Create tenant-owned custom roles.
- Update tenant-owned role metadata.
- Change tenant-owned role scope.
- Activate/deactivate tenant-owned roles.
- Hide/unhide System Roles for that tenant.

3. Authorized Customer Master operator:
- View applicable selectable roles.
- Assign roles to relationships only when separately authorized to perform relationship operations.

Additional constraints:
- Catalog management does not imply relationship assignment authority.
- Relationship assignment does not imply catalog management authority.
- Business relationship roles do not grant IAM permissions or administrative authority.
- No authority may physically delete roles or modify existing roleId/roleCode.
- Backend authorization enforcement is mandatory.
- Exact IAM roles, permission identifiers, grants, technical enforcement and actor mapping remain OPEN.
- Preserve existing approved scope-change safeguards.

Mandatory Audit coverage:
- System Role creation.
- Tenant Role creation.
- Label and description changes.
- Scope changes.
- Activation and deactivation.
- Tenant Hide/Unhide.
- System catalog publication.
- Unauthorized attempts to modify the catalog.

Reason policy:
- Optional for ordinary creation, metadata changes, compatible scope changes, activation, deactivation, Hide and Unhide.
- Mandatory for scope changes incompatible with existing relationships.
- Mandatory for system catalog publication, including the release reference.
- Preserve previously approved exception reason rules.

Logical Audit information:
- Event ID.
- Actor ID or authorized system identity.
- Tenant ID when applicable.
- Role ID and roleCode when available.
- Role origin.
- Operation.
- Previous and new values, when applicable.
- Reason, according to the operation.
- Timestamp.
- Outcome.
- Correlation ID.

Audit constraints:
- Catalog managers and ordinary users must not be able to modify or delete Audit history.
- Tenant Audit records must remain isolated.
- Historical records must survive changes to role titles, status and scope.
- Do not report a state-changing operation as successful unless durable Audit recording can be guaranteed.
- Ordinary catalog reads do not independently require product-level Audit under this decision.
- Security monitoring obligations remain unaffected.
- Unauthorized attempts must not disclose protected cross-tenant information.
- Exact Audit schema, transactional guarantees, storage, retention, recovery and access contracts remain OPEN.

Business Owner for FR-BJ-001: Farzad. Product requirements decision authority: Farzad. Interim accountable authority for Audit failure, ingestion, recovery and reconciliation policy: Farzad, until a separate owner is designated. Software development team is responsible for technical design and implementation. Preserve existing project governance authorities. Do not infer IAM permissions from these assignments.

Customer Operator: customer registration and maintenance. Customer Reviewer: authorized customer search and review. Customer Catalog Manager: authorized tenant role catalog management. Customer Verifier: independently authorized identity verification. Audit Reviewer: independently authorized review of Audit evidence. A person may hold multiple independent responsibilities. These are logical business responsibilities, not approved IAM role definitions or permission grants. Prepare an operation/resource/disclosure matrix; exact unresolved grants and disclosure boundaries remain OPEN rather than inventing authorization decisions.

INCLUDED: Individual customer registration; Company customer registration; Customer information maintenance; Contact channel management; Branch management; Related Person management; Relationship management; Role Catalog management; Basic duplicate detection; Customer search and review; Activation and deactivation. CONDITIONALLY INCLUDED: Customer archive and restoration, subject to approved dependency rules and available evidence; Manual identity verification, subject to approved evidence, issuer, authorization and SoD rules. DEFERRED: Real external identity verification integration; Executable Branch transfer coordination workflow; Advanced intelligent/fuzzy duplicate detection. EXCLUDED FROM CM-1: Customer merge; Physical customer deletion; Pending Submission or draft workflow; Direct external customer access. PROHIBITED: Offline operation. Preserve approved Branch transfer semantics: no automatic migration of relationships, activities or historical records. Do not remove deferred capabilities from the roadmap.

decisions.topic: Synthetic development scope and unresolved applicability
decisions.rule: Synthetic data only. No real customer information or identity documents. Preserve Tenant isolation and all architecture/security controls. Local development does not authorize production. Deployment profile selection and applicability of the nine conditional roadmap branches remain OPEN until explicitly decided. Do not invent profile selection or waive applicable roadmap requirements.

Company: Company name required; English name optional; Official identifier conditional; Registration number optional at registration; Telephone, Email, Address, Country, Website and Notes optional. Person: Given name and Family name required; English name optional; Official identifier conditional; Telephone, Email, Address, Country and Notes optional. Official identifiers are required only for workflows requiring formal identity verification. Optional fields must be validated when supplied. Preserve the existing field dictionary; do not silently remove previously approved fields.

Support an extensible jurisdiction-aware logical model. Initial Company identifier vocabulary: Iranian legal entity national identifier; Company registration number; Economic identifier. Initial Person vocabulary: Iranian national identifier; Passport number; Valid foreign national identifier. Multiple official identifiers may belong to one entity. Validation depends on identifier type, jurisdiction and issuing authority. Verified valid identifiers are unique within the applicable Tenant and identifier namespace; no global cross-Tenant deduplication. Definite verified identifier conflicts cannot be overridden; resolution requires authorized controlled correction. Exact issuer namespaces, normalization and technical validation mechanisms remain OPEN. Do not claim legal identifier formats or issuer validity without authoritative evidence.

decisions.topic: Basic duplicate signals and controlled exception
decisions.rule: Same verified valid official identifier blocks a definite conflict. Same unverified official identifier, same company name, same given and family name, same telephone, or same email produces a warning. Multiple matching signals have higher warning priority. Non-definitive signals are not identity proof. Preserve reuse of an existing record or authorized new registration with mandatory reason and Audit; no supervisor approval. Advanced algorithms, scoring thresholds, indexes and concurrent matching remain technical OPENs. Customer merge and physical deletion are excluded from CM-1.

Mandatory reason for changes to Official company name, Official person given/family name, Official identifiers, Identifier type, and Issuing authority. Reverification is required when a change invalidates or materially affects prior verification evidence. Ordinary telephone, email and address changes do not require a mandatory reason by default, but may require reverification when they formed part of the prior verification basis. Preserve optimistic concurrency and prior Audit rules.

decisions.topic: Relationship editing, termination and calendar-day semantics
decisions.rule: Person identity, Company/Branch target and Role identity are immutable during ordinary Relationship editing; correct them by ending the existing Relationship and creating a new Relationship. Manual END requires mandatory reason and Audit; natural expiry does not require a manually supplied END reason. Business time is calendar-day based; applicable time reference must be explicit and its exact selection remains OPEN. Preserve half-open [start,end), permit future start dates and optional end date; preserve controlled overlap exception rules. Prohibit new operational assignments to inactive Persons, Companies or Branches. Preserve existing Relationships/history after deactivation; history retention does not authorize retrospective assignment workflows. Calendar presentation, storage representation, locking and conflict-set mechanisms remain OPEN.

Applicable open dependencies blocking archive include Open sales opportunities, Active contracts, Open orders, Open support tickets, Active projects, Ongoing tenders, Outstanding delivery commitments, Open activities or follow-ups, Active branches, and Active relationships. Only applicable capabilities participate. Closed activities and historical records do not independently prevent archiving. Unknown dependency results are not clearance. Deactivation with open dependencies remains permitted under existing new-activity restrictions. Do not invent integrations with unimplemented services; if dependency clearance cannot be established, the affected archive operation remains blocked.

Reactivation requires mandatory-field validation, definite identifier conflict validation, authorization and Audit. VERIFIED identity is not globally required unless an applicable workflow requires it. Reason is optional for ordinary reactivation. No automatic activation of related branches or relationships. Preserve ARCHIVED -> INACTIVE -> ACTIVE; no direct ARCHIVED -> ACTIVE.

Permitted conceptual methods: review of valid identity documents; review of valid company registration documents; authorized manual verification with evidence; trusted system verification as a future integration. Verification without evidence is prohibited. Contact information or unsupported customer assertions alone are not formal identity proof. Record logical Evidence type, Issuing authority, Verifying authority, Timestamp, Outcome and Evidence reference. Exact approved issuer/evidence catalogs and applicable legal requirements remain OPEN. Do not authorize real document processing before these requirements are resolved. Initial development remains synthetic-only.

An actor separately authorized for registration and verification may perform ordinary registration and ordinary verification. A different authorized verifier is mandatory for Verification following correction of an already verified official identifier; Resolution and verification of a definite identifier conflict; Reverification after fundamental evidence invalidation. Additional legal/contractual SoD obligations remain applicable when established. Ordinary registration authority does not grant verification authority.

Preserve NOT_VERIFIED, VERIFIED and REQUIRES_REVERIFICATION. Initial identity state NOT_VERIFIED; successful verification with valid evidence VERIFIED; material identity change or expired/invalidated essential evidence REQUIRES_REVERIFICATION; proven fundamentally invalid verification NOT_VERIFIED; successful authorized reverification VERIFIED. A dispute or objection does not automatically restore VERIFIED. Preserve verification/invalidation history; no universal fixed expiry. Record and verification lifecycles remain independent.

decisions.topic: Customer mutation Audit coverage and reason policy
decisions.rule: All Customer Master mutations and unauthorized mutation attempts require Audit. Reason REQUIRED for Exceptional duplicate registration, Sensitive identity changes, Customer deactivation, Customer archive, Customer restoration, Branch deactivation, Exceptional Relationship overlap, Manual Relationship termination and Manual identity verification revocation. Reason OPTIONAL for Ordinary customer registration, Ordinary non-sensitive updates, Ordinary reactivation, Branch creation, Ordinary non-sensitive Branch updates, Ordinary Relationship creation/editing. Verification/reverification require valid evidence. Preserve stricter previously approved reasons. Role Catalog Audit remains governed by CM1-PD-073..077 and existing approved policies. Ordinary customer reads do not automatically require product-level Audit. Access to sensitive identity evidence and Audit records must be traceable and independently authorized.

decisions.topic: Logical Customer Audit information and minimization
decisions.rule: Logical Audit information: Event ID; Tenant ID when applicable; Actor ID; Actor type; Resource type; Resource ID when available; Operation; Previous values when applicable; New values when applicable; Reason where required or provided; Timestamp; Outcome; Correlation ID; Evidence reference where applicable. Avoid unnecessary sensitive data, credentials, tokens and complete identity documents in Audit records. No cross-Tenant disclosure. Preserve prior catalog-specific origin/identity/release and historical information requirements; no physical event schema is selected.

Durable Audit obligation is mandatory. Do not report mutation success if it cannot be guaranteed; unknown Audit outcome must not be reported as definite success. Central Audit unavailability may permit continuation only under an explicitly approved bounded policy; no automatic fail-open and no executable continuation policy authorized by this task. Prevent unauthorized Audit modification/deletion and treat attempts as security events. Preserve producer publication obligation versus authoritative ingestion evidence. Transactions, reliable publication, retry, recovery and reconciliation contracts remain OPEN.

Preserve inactive/archived Customer records; inactive Branch records/historical associations; ENDED Relationships/history; verification/revocation history; evidence references subject to applicable policy; protected Audit history; permanent Role identity/roleCode reservation under prior catalog decisions. Physical Customer deletion excluded from CM-1. Do not infer unlimited retention of personal data. Exact durations, legal hold, disclosure, evidence retention and regulatory applicability remain OPEN. No real customer information or identity evidence in initial synthetic development.

Operator: ordinary customer create/update, Branch/Relationship management and general read; independent explicit authority for duplicate exception, activation/deactivation, archive/restore. Reviewer: general read; Catalog Manager: selectable roles and own-Tenant role catalog; Verifier: general read and verification, separate authority for revocation/evidence; Audit Reviewer: authorized Audit review only. Operator/Reviewer/Catalog Manager may view selectable roles. General customer read includes contact and verification status; official identifiers masked absent independent identity-field access; Branch/Relationship require relevant resource access; evidence content and business history require independent authority; Audit access separately authorized. Deny by default, no foreign-Tenant disclosure, warnings limited to authorized facts, Backend authorization mandatory; no IAM grants.

Shared SaaS using Shared Cell is selected for initial synthetic development and testing. Dedicated Managed and Dedicated Sovereign are deferred for independent profile evidence; compatible business semantics and isolation in all profiles, no cross-profile acceptance inference. Preserve Sovereign local authority and no mandatory synchronous Central dependency.

Gateway/BFF and Feature Eligibility included for integrated product path; Quota deferred unless mandatory platform obligation; Operational Aggregation deferred, baseline health monitoring preserved; Durable Scheduling deferred unless selected operation needs it; Numeric Objectives required to be determined during design/testing; In-App Notification and Approved Reports excluded from CM-1; Attachments included specifically for Customer evidence. No roadmap changes, waiver, or automatic execution authorization.

Tenant-configurable document types, no code release needed for additions. Stable document ID and fixed unique document code; Persian title, optional English title, description, applicability PERSON/COMPANY/BOTH, mandatory/optional stage, single/multiple files, permitted formats, maximum size within platform bounds, expiry-date applicability, ACTIVE/INACTIVE, display order. Example document types are illustrative, not global obligations. Exact code grammar/namespace, configuration storage and platform file limits OPEN.

decisions.topic: Document requirement stage and change policy
decisions.rule: Tenant can require a document at initial registration or identity verification, or leave optional; default no mandatory initial registration documents. Add mandatory type or change optional to mandatory for subsequent applicable operations; mandatory to optional removes obligation; deactivate prevents new uploads for that type while preserving existing documents; rename retains identity; no physical deletion of type. Configuration changes do not automatically invalidate prior verification. Actual policy/legal prerequisites remain applicable.

Include authorized upload/view of one or multiple identity/company registration files as configured; record type, files, document number if needed, issue date, expiry when applicable, issuer, notes, uploader, upload date and version history. Replacement preserves prior versions. Upload alone does not set VERIFIED; independent authorized manual review with evidence and SoD still required. No OCR, automatic authenticity checking, external verification, general document-management or independent per-document approval workflow; expiry notifications deferred. File security and protected access mandatory; real evidence prohibited in initial synthetic development.

Show NOT_PROVIDED, PROVIDED, EXPIRED, SUPERSEDED, INVALIDATED. PROVIDED denotes upload, not authenticity. INVALIDATED by authorized user; replacement retains historical SUPERSEDED version. Show completed mandatory documents versus total applicable mandatory documents, separately from verification status. Exact computation for stage, expiry/invalidity, zero denominator and precedence remains OPEN where not expressly settled; no new verification shortcuts.

Independent authority for catalog management, upload/replacement/customer-document management, and view/download. Catalog, upload, replacement and other mutations and access to sensitive documents require Audit; no automatic rights from other responsibilities. Preserve durable Audit and evidence minimization constraints. File storage, malware controls, authorization mappings, lifecycle/retention and recovery contracts remain OPEN.

Tenant-configurable timezone; initial Iran timezone Asia/Tehran. Relationship business dates are calendar days in Tenant timezone, half-open [start,end), future starts/open ends permitted. Issue/expiry of documents are calendar dates; date-only facts do not shift with timezone. Events and Audit timestamps UTC; user-local presentation and Persian/Gregorian calendar configurable independently of language. Preserve past business dates when Tenant timezone changes, and event history unchanged. Exact timezone-change effective evaluation and storage mechanisms OPEN.

Company name and Branch name required 1–255 characters; Person given/family names required 1–100 each; English name optional max 255; address max 1000, notes max 4000. Unicode, trim leading/trailing whitespace; preserve original display and normalized search/match representation. Phone supports domestic/international numbers, email structure, website HTTP/HTTPS, country catalog, province/city and postal validation per country. Optional fields validated if supplied; no uniqueness of names/phone/email. Backend validation mandatory. Exact character-count/normalization, country dataset and official identifier legal formats OPEN; structural validation is not identity proof.

Permit multiple phones, emails and addresses; allow designation of primary phone, primary email and primary address, and contact channel type. Removal/deactivation preserves required history and Audit. No new mandatory contact or address; exact primary replacement, contact type vocabulary and retention mechanisms OPEN.
